scenes.text: A rocket heading for the Moon was struck by lightning. Twice.
It happened on November fourteenth, nineteen sixty nine, when Apollo twelve launched from Florida.
On board were Pete Conrad, Richard Gordon and Alan Bean.
Thirty six and a half seconds after liftoff, lightning hit the giant Saturn Five rocket.
Inside the spacecraft, warning lights lit up all over the control panel.
All three fuel cells dropped off line, and the crew thought they had lost power.
Then, at fifty two seconds, a second strike knocked out the guidance platform.
Down in Mission Control, the data screens turned into gibberish.
But a young flight controller named John Aaron remembered seeing a similar strange pattern during a test a year earlier.
He suggested one tiny fix: switch S C E to auxiliary.
Few people even knew that obscure switch.
Alan Bean remembered, flipped it, and the data came back.
Engineers later concluded the rocket itself had probably triggered the lightning by flying through charged clouds.
Five days later, Conrad and Bean landed safely on the Moon.
They even walked over to an old robot probe, Surveyor three.
Would you have stayed calm in that cockpit?

title: Apollo 12 was struck by lightning twice after launch ⚡
caption: On Nov 14, 1969, lightning hit Apollo 12 at 36.5 and 52 seconds after liftoff. One switch, 'SCE to AUX', saved the mission. 🚀
